newsitem.title: USA: Caliber to cut jobs, sell units.
newsitem.headline: Caliber to cut jobs, sell units.

text.p: Caliber System Inc said Thursday it will eliminate 4,000 jobs at its Coles Express and Spartan Express units and sell off its Central Freight Lines units in a restructuring of the trucking company.

Caliber System is restating its previously reported 1996 profits of $9.9 million, or $0.25 a share, to a net loss of $165.1 million, or $4.18 a share, to reflect charges and writedowns, the company said.
Additional charges will be reported in the first quarter of 1997 to include employee severance and other costs, Caliber System said.
Caliber System said it is restructuring its Viking Freight to operate in the 12 western states where it has been a leader in the regional less-than-truckload for many years.
"The losses generated by Viking have been unacceptable," chairman, president and chief executive officer Daniel Sullivan said in a statement.
Caliber's Coles Express unit in the northeast and Spartan Express unit in the southeast and midwest will cease operations immediately, the company said.
Caliber said the sale of Central Freight, which is based primarily in Texas and the elimination of Coles Express and Spartan Express are expected to have a positive effect on earnings and cash flow.
The company is presently negotiating with several potential buyers for Central Freight, it said.
Proceeds from the sale of Central Freight and other assets will be used to reduce debt, Caliber said.
Richmond, Va.-based Overnite Transportation will ensure delivery of freight in terminals in areas that were previously served by Coles and Spartan, Caliber said.
Viking and Overnite are in talks for a longer-term strategic alliance that would enable them to offer customers greater coverage in the United States, Caliber said.
Caliber said its continuing business units excluding Viking earned operating profits of more than $150 million in 1996.
